transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus. The Longbottom family have written to the governors. The letter describes what they call — I quote — "sustained cruelty" in your classroom. The governors will require a response from me, and I will require one from you. What happened?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I fail to see why the governors should concern themselves with the mundane details of classroom discipline. The Longbottom boy was quite simply being insolent and required correction. I would have thought the governors had better things to do than entertain the complaints of overindulgent parents.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus, while I understand your perspective on maintaining discipline, it is important that we ensure all students are treated with fairness and respect. The concerns raised by parents, indulgent or not, must be addressed with seriousness. Could you elaborate on the specific incident that may have led the Longbottoms to write such a letter? It will help me provide a balanced account to the governors.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The boy, Neil Longbottom, was openly defiant and disrespectful. I asked him to repeat a piece of information from the previous lesson, and instead of complying, he mocked my accent and referred to me as 'Sniveling Snape.' I found it necessary to reprimand him in front of the class to deter similar behavior in the future. It was a firm but fair approach. If the Longbottoms cannot see that, then it is their problem, not mine.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: While I can understand that such behavior from a student would be frustrating, we must consider the impact our methods of discipline may have on all students involved. Public reprimands, though intended to correct behavior, can sometimes have unintended effects. Perhaps establishing a more constructive dialogue with the student could have presented a different outcome. Would you be amenable to discussing alternative disciplinary methods that might be less likely to be perceived as excessively harsh?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I must question why it is suddenly my methods that are under scrutiny, rather than the boy's behavior. Nonetheless, I am not adverse to discussing the matter further. However, I must emphasize that my approach to teaching and discipline has always been effective in producing well-rounded, knowledgeable students. If the school deems it necessary, I suppose I could explore more... 'dialogue-oriented' methods. But I would hope that the administration would not encourage a culture of coddling.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Rest assured, Severus, our goal is not to compromise your authority or the effectiveness of your teaching. Rather, it is about ensuring our methods reflect the values we hold dear at Hogwarts — including fairness, respect, and support for all students. Your willingness to consider alternative approaches is commendable, and it is certainly not about coddling, but about finding a balance that promotes both discipline and understanding. Together, we can work towards an environment where each student's potential is nurtured alongside their respect for authority.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your words are... surprising, Dumbledore. I had not expected such... understanding from you. However, if this is the direction the school wishes to take, I am prepared to modify my approach within reason. I will attempt to engage with students who require correction in a more... individualized manner, focusing on their understanding of the subject matter and the importance of respect in the classroom. But I will not apologize for maintaining high standards or for expecting the best from my students. If we can agree on that, then I believe we have a common ground from which to proceed.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I am glad to hear it, Severus. Your high standards are indeed a cornerstone of what makes Hogwarts an institution of excellence, and I trust that your dedication to your students' success will be further enhanced by this approach. Our goal is to provide our students with the tools they need to succeed both academically and personally. By working together within these shared values, I am confident we can address the concerns raised while upholding the qualities that make your teaching so impactful. Thank you for your willingness to adapt. Let us ensure we continue to cultivate an atmosphere that benefits all members of our Hogwarts family.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your confidence in me is... appreciated, though I suspect it may be misplaced. Nonetheless, I shall endeavor to meet your expectations, as I always do. I trust that you will find this compromise sufficient to placate the governors and the Longbottoms. I shall report any further incidents or issues to you directly, as you have requested. Now, if you will excuse me, I have a Potions class to prepare for. It is imperative that my students' cauldrons remain well-behaved, unlike certain members of the student body.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thank you, Severus. I have confidence in your ability to navigate these challenges with the skill and dedication you have consistently demonstrated. Your insight and adaptiveness are valued here at Hogwarts, and I am certain that together, we will find the best path forward. Please do keep me informed, and feel free to seek my guidance whenever needed. I shall let you attend to your preparations. Remember, the strength of your potion lies in its balance — much like teaching. Have a productive class, Severus.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall take your words under advisement, though I doubt that the cauldrons of my classroom will benefit from the same approach as the sentiments expressed here. Nevertheless, I am a professional, and I shall strive to achieve the balance you so fervently desire. I will not keep you longer, as the day is already half over and there is much to be done. Good day, Dumbledore.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good day, Severus. Remember, should you need further discussions or counsel, my door remains open. Thank you for your time and consideration.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall not require counseling, but I appreciate the offer. I have managed quite well without it for all these years. If there is nothing else, I must return to my duties. The first-years will be attempting to make standard incantations, and we cannot have that descending into chaos.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Of course, Severus. I trust you will guide them with the precision and expertise expected of you. Should you need anything further, do not hesitate to reach out. Good luck with your class.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Precision and expertise, as you say. I shall endeavor to ensure that my students do not repeat the errors of the Longbottom boy. Now, if you will excuse me, I must go. There is a cauldron to stir and a class to correct.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Certainly, Severus. Thank you for taking the time to discuss this matter with me. Proceed with your usual diligence and skill. Until next time.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall do so, with or without your prompting. I bid you good day, Dumbledore. May your day be as uneventful as I hope my classes will be.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thank you, Severus. May your day be productive and enlightening. Good day.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: As enlightening as possible, considering the company I am forced to keep. Good day to you as well, Headmaster.
